subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs implicitly use delete-after-run cleanup, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only lifecycle flag?
rationale: The PR's defaulting direction conflicts with an open strict-validation PR, and the right upgrade behavior for existing omitted jobs depends on that lifecycle contract.

options.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this direction, but require a persisted/load or doctor path for existing omitted jobs before merge.

options.title: Adopt one-shot-only deleteAfterRun
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after its Gateway/UI compatibility blockers are resolved.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Merge the new default only for newly normalized jobs and explicitly document that existing omitted jobs need operator or doctor action.

recommendation.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this direction, but require a persisted/load or doctor path for existing omitted jobs before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The current normalization and store-preservation lines route through recent cron/store history attributed to this person, and those files are central to either contract.
